composers.name: Enric Morera i Viura
composers.why: Wikidata: Catalan composer, born 22 May 1865, as in the article. IMSLP has the same dates, lists "Enric (Enrique) Morera i Viura" and the same VIAF cluster (44491201). GND, LoC and BnF all give 1942; the day differs (11 or 12 March), which does not matter. The GND search also returns a namesake born 1959: choose the record by dates and occupation. The Identifiers section of the Wikidata page links GND, LoC, BnF and VIAF; cite the record you opened, not Wikidata. Style: the Gran Enciclopèdia de la Música, a national music encyclopaedia, says he built on Catalan folk song, "sempre reinterpretat, mai copiat", and that his sardanas and choral works were played everywhere: national_folk first. His harmony began under Wagner's influence, La fada is "de clara influència wagneriana", and his lowered scale degrees are a "recurs propi del Romanticisme tardà": late_romantic, which by language is also the period. Modernisme here is the Catalan art movement of about 1890–1910, not musical modernism; he was "refractari a les innovacions tècniques", so no 20th-century movement tag.

composers.name: Ernestina Lecuona y Casado

worked.notes: No dates in GND or LoC; Wikipedia, Wikidata and IMSLP agree on 3 Sep 1951.
worked.style_source: EcuRed (a wiki; no reference-level entry is free online) https://www.ecured.cu/Ernestina_Lecuona

composers.why: IMSLP files her under the first surname only (Spanish double surname); the category lists "Lecuona y Casado" as an alternate name, the same dates and the same Wikidata item. Category:Lecuona,_Ernesto is her brother. GND has no record and LoC one without dates, so the date comes from level 2: the Dictionnaire universel des créatrices, which cites the New Grove Dictionary of Women Composers. Style: her output is Cuban song genres (habaneras, criollas, guajiras, danzones, sones and "sobre todo, boleros", EcuRed, which cites Giro's Diccionario enciclopédico de la música en Cuba): national_folk. The dated boleros are from 1932 and 1936, and the bolero is a 20th-century idiom, so the period is early_20th_century, not romantic; her first piece (Luisa, 1897) does not carry the bulk. EcuRed is a wiki, so say so in style_source; with library access, the Norton/Grove Dictionary of Women Composers (1994) is the level-1 source.

works.work_id: Suite for 2 Violins and Small Orchestra, Op.15 (Zilcher, Hermann)
works.title: Suite for 2 Violins and Small Orchestra, Op.15
works.why: The original is two soloists with orchestra. The only files are a version for 2 violins and piano under Arrangements and Transcriptions; judge the original, and even a composer's own chamber version (7) loses to concerto (9). Arrangement files still count for has_files. No category is a rights category (Sibley Mirroring Project is a scan source). Its form is suite: concerto as a form needs the title, so the family stays concerto while the form is suite.

works.title: Caprice No.2
works.why: Violin alone. A complete score (PWM, 1952) is on the page. The category list has WorkNonPD-USandEU; the file's "Copyright: Public Domain" line is IMSLP's Canadian status, and the basis comes from the categories. IMSLP files it under Caprices, which is not a listed form, so the form is none.
